## How this order is derived

`docs/requirements.yaml` is keyed by requirement ID, so reading it in file
order groups requirements by function prefix. That is not a build order.
This file is the build order, derived from the dependency signals that
actually exist in the register:

| Signal | Trust | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `> **Extends:** X` in a body | hard | X must be built first. Verified acyclic. |
| `depends_on` between platform workflows | hard | expanded to every requirement pair across the two workflows |
| `stage` | ordering intent | breaks ties **within** a wave only; stage numbers were assigned per feature area and do not form a global order |
| `**See:**` | related, not dependent | **not** used as an edge -- it contains real cycles. Reported as advisory context by `depsort path`. |

A requirement that is `RELEASED` or `DEPRECATED` counts as a satisfied
prerequisite and is not scheduled here (302 of 350 requirements).

## How to read a wave

Everything in wave N has all of its prerequisites in waves below N. A wave
is **not** a stage -- it is "what is unblocked now". Within a wave there is
no ordering constraint, so its requirements may be batched to WF-02 in any
order, or in parallel, subject to the WF-02 batch cap of 4.

```bash
python3 tools/depsort.py order          # this file, live
python3 tools/depsort.py path MIG-03    # what must precede a requirement
python3 tools/depsort.py check          # cycles and dangling references
python3 tools/wfctl.py next             # the same question at workflow level
```
